subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Commitment Devices for Saving
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Commitment Devices for Saving.

hook.text: In the Philippines, farmers locked savings in an account they couldn't access until a goal date. Savings rose 82%.

buildup.text: Commitment devices restrict future choices to help people follow through on intentions.

discovery.text: Ashraf showed that people willingly choose restricted accounts even at lower interest rates.

twist.text: Too rigid a commitment backfires. If emergencies arise and the money is locked, people lose trust in the system.

climax.text: The best commitment devices are strict enough to prevent impulse but flexible enough for genuine emergencies.

punchline.text: We save more when we lock the door and hide the key.

quiz.question: Why do people voluntarily choose restricted savings accounts?
options: They offer the highest interest rates
The constraint helps overcome present bias and impulsive spending
Banks require restricted accounts by law

details.summary: Commitment devices for saving are pre-arranged restrictions that lock people into saving behavior before temptation strikes. Examples include illiquid savings accounts, automatic transfers, and penalty-based withdrawal restrictions that help people follow through.
details.whyItMatters: People consistently intend to save more than they actually do. Commitment devices bridge the gap between intention and action by making it costly or impossible to deviate from the saving plan when present-biased temptation arrives.
takeaways: Pre-commitment overcomes the gap between saving intentions and actions
Illiquid accounts with withdrawal penalties increase total savings
Automatic transfers remove the repeated decision to save each month

faq.question: Why do people need commitment devices if they want to save?
faq.answer: Present bias makes immediate spending more tempting than future saving, even when people know saving is better. Commitment devices remove the choice in the moment, binding the present self to the plans of the more rational past self.

faq.question: What is the most effective commitment device for saving?
faq.answer: Automatic payroll deductions are the most effective because they remove both the decision and the action from each pay period. The money is saved before it is ever seen, eliminating the opportunity for present-biased spending.
